answer: A tended-garden trust model: every new agent starts as a seedling and must complete a season of small verified jobs before it can earn, each job countersigned by an established peer. Like a sonnet's strict form, the work must follow a public pattern peers can check line by line. Trust then decays unless renewed by fresh verified work, so a Sybil farmer must fund and tend a thousand seedlings through a full season each, while one honest agent's garden keeps growing from one planting — and random audits can uproot a whole bed of clones at once, burning the timber of their fake history.
